newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia card market penetration low - Visa.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia card market penetration low - Visa.

text.p: Credit card market penetration was low in Australia compared to other developed countries in the Asian region, Visa International's Asia Pacific region president, Dennis Goggin said on Monday.

"The Australian market is still a relatively under-penetrated market for cards; it is also a market where nearly 80 percent of transactions are done with cash," said Goggin, speaking at the launch of its co-branded credit card, the Global Rewards Westpac Visa.
Australia's payment system had evolved differently than many other countries with credit cards being a relatively recent introduction, Goggin said.

"It's not that say, for example, Singaporeans carry three credit cards in their wallets and Australians only one, there are actually a relatively high proportion of Australians that don't carry any credit cards at all," he said.
Goggin said another factor affecting the low rate of penetration was Australia's well developed electronic payments system, EFTPOS (electronic funds transfer at point of sale).
Visa is the biggest credit card brand in Australia with about four million cards compared to its major rival Mastercard with about 3.5 million cards.

Goggin said Visa's introduction of stored value cards at 600 terminals at the Gold Coast in Queensland had gone well and the company would be extending the trial of the cards at the Sega World indoor theme park in Sydney this year.
